articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea.

In addition to the designations and removals, OFAC issued new general licenses pertaining to Iran and Russia. The agency also published amended Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance on these updated measures.
These actions reflect ongoing adjustments to U.S. sanctions programs in response to evolving geopolitical considerations and specific activities in the targeted regions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026. These designations target entities involved in the alleged theft of trade secrets, particularly impacting five Chinese companies.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued associated general licenses to provide guidance and authorization for certain transactions. China has strongly urged the U.S. to lift these sanctions, warning of potential countermeasures to protect its enterprises' legitimate rights and interests.

The Chinese Ministry of Commerce stated that the U.S. actions seriously infringe upon the rights of Chinese companies and are egregious in nature, emphasizing that the rapid development of Chinese AI companies stems from their commitment to research and innovation, not trade secret theft.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License and FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question on October 16, 2026. This amendment, specifically GL 60A, extends the authorization for transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela until April 21, 2027, superseding the original October 23, 2026, end date.
This action follows a series of adjustments to Venezuela sanctions, including the recent delisting of a prominent Venezuelan politician.
The continuous modifications reflect the U.S. government's evolving approach to sanctions in Venezuela, balancing humanitarian concerns with broader policy objectives.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Cuba Entity, and Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation on October 15, 2026. This action targets efforts to move revenues from Iran's oil sales through a clandestine banking system, including a Hong Kong entity, Elitesphere Trading Co. Limited, for its alleged ties to Iran.

The Cuba designation targeted Banco Internacional de Comercio, S.A. (BICSA), a Cuban state-owned bank, for operating in the financial services sector of the Cuban economy and for allegedly providing services to an Iranian financial institution.
OFAC also issued new and amended general licenses and Frequently Asked Questions, reflecting a broader U.S. effort to target alleged financial links between Cuba and Iran.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Steptoe / HKTDC Research

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuela-Related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of a Venezuela-related designation on October 14, 2026. Jorge Rodriguez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, was delisted from OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list.
This action ends the associated asset freeze and removes obstacles for U.S. persons dealing with him. Rodriguez was initially designated in 2018.
The delisting is part of Washington's latest push for diplomacy and expansion of energy investment in Venezuela.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Al Jazeera / Steptoe

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism designations on October 13, 2026. These designations targeted four individuals and 11 entities allegedly linked to Cartel del Noreste (CDN), a Mexico-based cartel.
This action represents OFAC's largest sanctions action to date targeting CDN, which is designated as both a Foreign Terrorist Organization and a Specially Designated Global Terrorist.
The designations were imposed pursuant to Executive Order 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, International Criminal Court Designation, and Burma-Related Designation Removal
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026. This settlement addresses alleged violations of OFAC sanctions programs.
In a separate action, OFAC announced a designation related to the International Criminal Court and issued associated general licenses. This designation reflects U.S. policy regarding the ICC.
Additionally, OFAC announced a Burma-related designation removal, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against entities connected to Burma.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026. This license, GL 135, authorizes certain transactions related to imports of Russian diesel fuel to the U.S. until April 7, 2027.

This action comes amidst broader discussions and actions regarding Russian sanctions, including a recent executive order waiving many sanctions and tariffs introduced by the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.
The issuance of this general license indicates a strategic move to manage global energy prices while maintaining pressure on Russia.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations and Amends Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 8, 2026. These designations are part of ongoing efforts to target Iran's financial and petroleum sectors.

Concurrently, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License and an amended Russia-related General License. The amended Russia-related General License, GL 128D and GL 130B, concerns certain activities involving Lukoil International GmbH and related entities, extending authorizations until April 24, 2027.
These actions underscore the U.S. government's continued focus on both Iranian and Russian sanctions programs, adapting them to current geopolitical and economic circumstances.

articles.headline: EU Adopts 22nd Sanctions Package Against Russia, Targeting Military-Industrial Complex
body: The Council of the European Union adopted its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia on October 12, 2026. This significant package primarily focuses on listings, adding 1,569 individuals and entities to the EU sanctions lists, comprising 826 Russian companies and 743 individuals.
The measures target a large number of companies and executives linked to Russia's defense industries, including suppliers of components used in missiles, drones, and aircraft.

Additionally, 77 political figures connected with the September 2026 elections in occupied Ukrainian territory were designated. This package is considered one of the most significant sanctions developments since 2022, bringing the total number of designations under the Ukraine-related sanctions regime to almost 4,600.
articles.source: Council of the European Union / Squire Patton Boggs / Mondaq

articles.headline: EU Sanctions Three Individuals and Four Entities for Supporting DPRK Weapons Programs and Russia Ties
body: The Council of the European Union adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and four entities on October 12, 2026, under its autonomous sanctions list on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK).

These designations target those responsible for supporting, promoting, or facilitating activities contributing to the DPRK's nuclear weapons, ballistic missiles, or other weapons of mass destruction programs, as well as for violating and evading United Nations sanctions.

The new listings specifically address activities linked to growing military and economic cooperation between the DPRK and Russia, including the deployment of DPRK workers in Russia and commercial and industrial cooperation.
articles.source: Council of the European Union / Consilium.europa.eu / NK News

articles.headline: EU Lists Individuals and Entities for Circumventing Sanctions Against Russia
body: The Council of the European Union adopted additional restrictive measures on October 15, 2026, targeting three individuals and nine entities involved in the import of sanctioned goods to Russia and the circumvention of EU sanctions related to oil and financial transactions.
These listings were adopted under the EU's restrictive measures framework targeting actions undermining or threatening Ukraine's territorial integrity, sovereignty, and independence.
Those designated are subject to an asset freeze, and the provision of funds or economic resources to them is prohibited. Listed individuals are also subject to an EU travel ban.

This significant penalty underscores the importance of robust compliance programs for financial institutions to prevent sanctions breaches across various regimes.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026, Including Significant BSA Violations
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released its enforcement actions for October 2026, highlighting significant deficiencies in Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance programs at several institutions.

Among the actions, a Cease and Desist Order and Civil Money Penalty were issued against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah, for BSA compliance program deficiencies, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence and customer identification program violations.

Additionally, a Civil Money Penalty of $750 million was assessed against Bank of America, National Association, Charlotte, North Carolina, for similar BSA compliance program deficiencies, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and sending wires with inaccurate transmittor name information.

articles.headline: OCC Issues Prohibition Orders Against Individuals for Embezzlement
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced prohibition orders against two individuals for embezzling customer funds in October 2026.
Jennifer Hamblin, a Vault Teller at a Cincinnati, Ohio, branch of Fifth Third Bank, N.A., was issued an Order of Prohibition for embezzling approximately $292,000 in customer funds.

Similarly, Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at the La Mirada, California Operations Center of U.S. Bank National Association, was prohibited for embezzling approximately $194,131 in bank customer funds.

articles.headline: OCC Report Finds Nine Largest Banks Engaged in Debanking Practices
body: On October 14, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released a report titled 'Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans,' which found that the nine largest national banks it supervises engaged in debanking practices.

The report concluded that between 2020 and September 2025, each of these banks maintained policies or practices that may have influenced the denial or limitation of financial services based on customers' political or religious beliefs or lawful business activities.

The OCC reviewed nearly 100,000 complaints and approximately 420,000 pages of bank documents, identifying broad reputation risk policies and industry-specific restrictions as contributing factors to these debanking practices.

body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. (bank), for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. This amount is the largest in OCC history.

articles.headline: FCC Blocks New Drone Authorizations for Devices with Covered List Components
body: Effective October 13, 2026, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will no longer authorize new devices, including drones assembled in the U.S., that contain logic-bearing parts made by companies on the FCC's Covered List, such as DJI or Autel.
This new rule, published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026, closes a previous gap that allowed U.S. assemblers to use components from listed companies and still obtain drone approval.

While existing DJI aircraft remain legal to fly and previously authorized models can still be sold, this action significantly impacts the market for new drone models and components, particularly for utility, public safety, and government buyers.
articles.source: Harris Aerial / Detect / Jeroen Van Nieuwenhove

articles.headline: Treasury Proposes Rule to Curb High-Tech Investments in Adversary Nations
body: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a new rule on October 23, 2026, aimed at curbing American high-tech investments in China, Russia, North Korea, Cuba, Iran, and other 'countries of concern.'

This rule expands restrictions to cover investments in hypersonic systems, supercomputing, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence, building upon an existing program that began in 2023 under then-President Joe Biden.
The proposed rule, which will undergo public comment before finalization, is intended to prevent U.S. capital from accelerating military-relevant capabilities in these nations.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

body: Unidentified gunmen on motorcycles swooped on a remote village on Friday, looting shops and setting houses ablaze.

articles.headline: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
body: Obama said the election was "the last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration".

articles.headline: More than 1,300 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
body: Hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations in France, with protests also taking place in other European countries.

articles.headline: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
body: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.

articles.headline: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
body: Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.

articles.headline: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
body: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

articles.headline: Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack
body: The independent MP is now in a serious but stable condition, according to the Melbourne hospital.

articles.headline: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
body: Three people - two women and one man - have been released, and one person remains in custody, gardaí say.

articles.headline: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
body: Kaylub Giamanco has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher.

articles.headline: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
body: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.

articles.headline: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
body: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.

articles.headline: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
body: Police have launched a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor after the multi-storey building collapsed while still under construction.

articles.headline: Trump administration sues to block certification of upcoming Alaska election
body: The justice department has filed a lawsuit arguing that the inclusion of two candidates named Dan Sullivan could confuse voters.

articles.headline: Fireworks and tear gas as protesters and riot police clash in Paris
body: The BBC's Europe correspondent reports from Paris where mostly peaceful protests turned into unrest after nightfall.
